intent: Report how many peaks peaks.bed contains (a standard 5-column BED file), their total width in bp, and the count and width per chromosome.
silent_error: pandas.read_csv uses header='infer' and a BED file has no header line, so the first peak (chrX:1030200-1030650) is consumed as the column names; renaming the columns afterwards hides it. The script reports 5 peaks instead of 6, the 450 bp of the lost peak are missing from the total, and chrX vanishes from the per-chromosome table. No exception or warning is raised; all remaining numbers are integers of the expected type.

files.summarize_peaks.py:
import pandas as pd

peaks = pd.read_csv("peaks.bed", sep="\t")
peaks.columns = ["chrom", "start", "end", "name", "score"]
peaks["width"] = peaks["end"] - peaks["start"]
print("n_peaks", len(peaks))
print("total_width", int(peaks["width"].sum()))
for chrom, sub in peaks.groupby("chrom", sort=True):
    print(chrom, len(sub), int(sub["width"].sum()))

import pandas as pd

peaks = pd.read_csv("peaks.bed", sep="\t", header=None, names=["chrom", "start", "end", "name", "score"])
peaks["width"] = peaks["end"] - peaks["start"]
print("n_peaks", len(peaks))
print("total_width", int(peaks["width"].sum()))
for chrom, sub in peaks.groupby("chrom", sort=True):
    print(chrom, len(sub), int(sub["width"].sum()))
